(b) As to the manager of the applicant's proposed premises (if not the same as the applicant), the same information as required of the applicant in this section.
(c) Each application for a license under this chapter shall be accompanied by a certified bank check for the full amount of the license fee, together with a separate certified bank check in the amount of $200.00 to defray investigative and administrative costs. If the applicant withdraws his application prior to its being submitted to the governing authority, or if the application is denied by the governing authority, the deposit representing the license fee shall be refunded, but the $200.00 paid for investigation and administrative costs shall not be refunded.
(d) The application shall be sworn to or affirmed under oath.
(e) Surveyor's certificate. Unless otherwise permitted by law, all new applications for each premises shall be accompanied by a current certificate from a registered surveyor and shall contain the following information about the applicant's premises:
(1) A scale drawing of the premises, with its location identified by street address and tax map and parcel number, and showing any structures on, or to be built on, the land;
(2) Any proposed off-street parking facilities and all outdoor lighting;
(3) Current zoning classification of the premises; and
(4) The distance in yards as measured by the most direct route of travel from the nearest property line of the premises to nearest property line of each of the following: any school building, school grounds, public housing authority, college campus or alcoholic treatment center which is owned and operated by the state or any county or municipal government.
(f) An application under this chapter containing known false information may result in the denial of the license applied for and prosecution as a felony.
(g) As a prerequisite to the issuance of any initial license only, the applicant shall furnish a complete set of fingerprints to be forwarded to the Georgia Bureau of Investigation, which shall search the files of the Georgia Crime Information Center for any instance of criminal activity during the two years immediately preceding the date of the application. The Georgia Bureau of Investigation shall also submit the fingerprints to the Federal Bureau of Investigation under the rules established by the United States Department of Justice for processing and identification of records. The federal record, if any, shall be obtained and returned to the governing authority submitting the fingerprints.
(h) Applications must be filed on or before November 30 of each year; otherwise, a penalty equal to 20 percent of the annual license fee shall be imposed.
(i) Except for temporary licenses or permits that may be granted pursuant to this chapter, all licenses shall be for the full calendar year or for the number of months (or portion thereof) remaining in the calendar year. License fees shall not be prorated for any reason, and license fees shall not be refundable for any reason.
(j) Failure to furnish complete information in the application will delay the issuance of the license. The failure to furnish complete information within 30 days after being requested to do so by the city clerk may be grounds to deny the application.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
148:
A license shall not be issued to any person unless it appears to the satisfaction of the governing authority that the license applicant is of good moral character. At the time an application is filed, the applicant shall, by affidavit duly sworn or affirmed, certify that he has not been convicted of or entered a guilty plea to any misdemeanor or felony involving moral turpitude, any lottery or gambling offense, or any offense related to illegal possession, distribution or sale of any illegal drug or substance (including, but not limited to marijuana or any narcotic) or liquor within five years of the filing of the application. A license shall not be issued to any applicant who has been convicted under any federal, state, or local law or entered a guilty plea to any misdemeanor or felony involving moral turpitude, any lottery or gambling offense, or any offense related to illegal possession, distribution or sale of any illegal drug or substance (including, but not limited to marijuana or any narcotic) or liquor within five years of the filing of the application.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
149:
(a) No applicant for a license shall be issued to any person who is not a citizen of the United States. No license for the retail sale or distribution of alcoholic beverages shall be granted to any person who is not a resident of Toombs County, Georgia, unless the applicant designates a Toombs County resident (such resident shall be an individual) who consents in writing to be responsible for any matter related to the license.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to sell, or possess for the purpose of sale, or offer to sell any alcoholic beverage within the city, except pursuant to a license as permitted by this chapter.
(c) A retail premises or business shall not have alcoholic beverages on its sales floor or in its cooler unless such premises or business has a license as permitted by this chapter.
(d) Any license issued under this chapter shall be a mere grant or privilege to carry on the business during the term of the license subject to all terms and conditions imposed by this chapter and state law.
(e) (1) A person shall apply for a license in the name of the person who owns and/or operates the licensed business, and upon approval, the license will be issued in the name of the person.
(2) Where an entity (e.g., corporations, limited liability companies, limited partnerships, limited liability partnerships, trusts, etc.), which is duly formed and in good standing with the Secretary of State, applies for a license, the entity shall apply in the legal name of the entity, and upon approval, the license shall be issued in the name of the entity; provided that, such applicant shall attach to the application a certificate showing compliance with the annual registration requirements from the Secretary of State, corporate division. showing the name and address of a registered agent for service within the state, and providing the identity of an agent, who is involved in the active management of the business to be licensed, who shall meet the requirements of individual applicants under this chapter at the time application is made and at all times during which the license is in effect.
(3) Where a partnership applies for a license, the partnership shall apply in the name of one of the general partners, who is a resident of this state, and upon approval, the license will be issued in the name of all partners of the partnership; if the applicant is a partner in a partnership, the requirements of this chapter shall apply to all partners at the time of application, and at all times during which the license is in effect.
(f) No license shall be issued to any person that has not attained the age of 21 years.
(g) No license shall be issued to any person who has had any license issued by the city revoked within the two years prior to the filing of an application as permitted by this chapter.
(h) The governing authority may decline to issue a license to any person that has violated any part of this chapter within one year prior to the filing of the application for such license.
(i) The governing authority may decline to issue a license where any person having any interest in or control over the licensee or licensed business or premises does not meet the same moral character requirements applicable to licensee, as set forth in this chapter.
(j) The governing authority may decline to issue a license when after reasonable effort the city clerk or chief of police is unable to verify any statement or information required to be disclosed in the application.
(k) Any person or entity who is issued a license shall have and continuously maintain a registered agent upon whom any process, notice or demand required or permitted by law or under this chapter may be served upon. The registered agent shall be a resident of Toombs County. The licensee shall file the name, address and telephone number of the registered agent, along with the written consent of such agent to receive any process, notice or demand required or permitted by law or under this chapter, with the city on such form as prescribed by the city clerk.
(l) No license shall be issued to any person until he provides the city clerk with proof of current commercial general liability insurance, covering the business and/or premises seeking the license, in the form of a true and correct insurance declarations page. Such proof must be provided annually to the city clerk.
(m) No license shall be issued to any person unless he personally appears before the governing authority at one regularly scheduled council meeting.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
150:
(a) An applicant who will operate more than one premises shall complete a separate application for each premises and shall pay all applicable license fees for each premises.
(b) Each license shall be personal to the licensee, and no license is transferable except as may otherwise be provided in this chapter.
(c) In the case of the death of a licensee, the deceased licensee's license shall be the property of his heirs or personal representatives, as the case may be, and the business or premises may continue to sell alcoholic beverages for a period of 45 days from the date of death of deceased licensee or until expiration of deceased licensee's license or until issuance of a new licensee, whichever occurs first, and upon such occurrence authorization to sell under the deceased licensee's license shall terminate by operation of law.
(d) If 50 percent or more of a licensed entity is to be sold or transferred to a person other than any existing partner, shareholder or member, then such licensed entity shall apply for a new license as set forth herein and pay all license costs and fees, if such licensed entity desires to be authorized, or continue to be authorized, to sell alcoholic beverages.
(e) Any licensee who desires to change the location of the licensed premises within the city shall so notify the city clerk in writing 30 business days prior to any such change of location. The notice of change of location shall be accompanied by a survey as required by this chapter. A licensee's business shall not change location unless the new location complies with all provisions of this chapter. The governing authority shall have the authority to approve or deny the change of location in the same manner that it may approve or deny the issuance of a new license. An investigative fee of $200.00 shall be paid by the licensee at the time that a notice of change of location is made. If a change of location is approved, with no change of ownership of the business, the license fee paid for the old location shall be applied to the new location.
(f) Any licensee who desires to change the name of his business or premises shall so notify the city clerk in writing at least 30 business days prior to any change of name, and the city clerk shall direct the issuance of a corrected license in replacement of the original license. A fee of $25.00 shall be paid by the licensee at the time that such notice given for the change of name of such business or premises.
(g) Any licensee who changes the manager of his business or premises shall so notify the city clerk in writing at least three days of the effective date of notice of the change of manager and shall file with the city clerk such information about the new manager as the city clerk may require. A fee of $25.00 shall be paid at the time that the notice for the change of manager is made to defer the costs of investigation and administration.
(h) Except as provided in this section, any change in the ownership or control of any licensed entity shall be grounds to revoke a license issued to such entity.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
151:
(a) No license shall be issued to any elected official of the city or any employee of the city, nor shall any such person have any whole, partial or beneficial interest in any license.
(b) No license shall be issued in connection with any premises that fails to meet: i) all applicable fire, life safety, building and health laws, rules and regulations under law or under the Code, and ii) all applicable zoning ordinances and regulations of the Code.
(c) No license shall be issued in connection with any premises in any city zoning district, except for commercial zoning districts within the city known as C-1 and C-2.
(d) No license shall be issued to any applicant who is delinquent in the payment of city taxes or fees, including, but not limited to property taxes, alcoholic beverage excise taxes, business license fees, occupational taxes, or any other tax or fee which is owed to the city by the applicant.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
152:
Where a person applies for a license in connection with any premises that is not yet in existence or completed, a license may be issued for such premises; provided that, the plans for such premises comply with this chapter and the Code. No sales shall be allowed in such premises until it has been completed in accordance with such plans, a certificate of occupancy issued, and it has been inspected by the proper state and/or local officials, including, but not limited to the city manager, city building inspector, city code enforcement officer or any sworn police officer of the city, to ensure compliance with this chapter and the Code.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
153:
(a) All licensed premises must open for business within six months after issuance of the license. Failure to do so shall serve as a ground for revocation of such license by the governing authority, unless an extension of time is granted by the governing authority before the expiration of the six-month period, for good cause shown by the licensee. No refund of the license fee shall be made in the event of a revocation hereunder.
(b) Any licensee who begins operating the business or premises authorized in the license, but who thereafter ceases operation for six months within any calendar year, shall be subject to revocation of his license by the governing authority, unless an extension of time is granted by the governing authority before the expiration of the six-month period, for good cause shown by the licensee. No refund of license fee shall be made in the event of a revocation hereunder.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
154:
(a) All licenses shall expire on December 31 of each year. A licensee who desires to renew the license shall file an application, with the requisite fees as set forth in this chapter, with the city clerk on the form provided for renewal of the license for the ensuing year. All applications for renewal will be reviewed by the governing authority or its designee. A licensee does not have a right to automatic renewal and must be compliant with this chapter when applying for the renewal of his license. Applications for renewal must be filed on or before November 30 of each year; otherwise, a penalty equal to 20 percent of the annual license fee shall be imposed. No renewal license shall be granted after December 31, but such application shall be treated as an initial application, and the applicant shall be required to comply with all rules and regulations for the granting of licenses as if no previous license had been issued to licensee.
(b) Except for temporary permits that may be granted pursuant to this chapter, all licenses granted under this chapter shall be for the full calendar year or for the number of months (or portion thereof) remaining in the calendar year. License fees shall not be prorated for any reason, and license fees shall not be refundable for any reason.
(c) Failure to furnish complete information in the renewal application will delay the issuance of the license. The failure to furnish complete information within 30 days after being requested to do so by the city clerk may be grounds to deny the renewal application.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
156:
In addition to any other punishment or penalty set forth in this chapter, unless prohibited by law, any person who violates any provision of this chapter may be cited for violating same and tried in the municipal court of the city, and upon conviction for any such violation, said court shall be authorized to punish such person by a fine not exceeding $300.00 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 30 days or any combination thereof. Further, with respect to violations of this chapter that are continuous with respect to time, each day the violation continues is a separate offense, and with respect to violations of this chapter that are not continuous with respect to time, each act constitutes a separate offense.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
157:
The city manager, code enforcement officers, building inspectors and sworn police officers of the city shall have the authority to inspect any business or premises licensed under this chapter during the hours in which the business or premises is open for business. These inspections shall be made for the purpose of verifying compliance with the requirements of this chapter and state law. This section is not intended to limit the authority of any other city officer to conduct inspections authorized by other provisions of this Code or state law.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
158:
(a) All licenses shall include a statement as to the type of license issued, the name of the licensee, and the name and address of the licensed business or premises. All licenses shall, at all times, be kept in plain view within the licensed business or premises.
(b) All licensees shall post in a prominent location on the licensed business or premises, in plain view of all individuals on the premises, an approved sign setting forth or summarizing the laws of the state and city regarding the sale of alcoholic beverages to underage or intoxicated persons. Each sign shall be of a size and configuration approved by the governing authority or its designee and include either the laws of the state and city regarding the sale of alcoholic beverages to underage or intoxicated persons, or summaries thereof, as approved by the city manager; provided that the city manager may design and have printed approved signs, which shall be made available to licensees for the cost of $75.00.
(c) Subject to all terms and conditions imposed by the state law and the Code, and all licenses shall have printed on the front these words: "THIS LICENSE IS A MERE PRIVILEGE SUBJECT TO BEING SUSPENDED OR REVOKED AND IS SUBJECT TO ANY FUTURE ORDINANCES WHICH MAY BE ENACTED."
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
159:
(a) No person under 18 years of age shall be employed in or about the premises of any person licensed to sell alcoholic beverages.
(b) It shall be unlawful for a person under 21 years of age to attempt to purchase an alcoholic beverage or for any person to purchase an alcoholic beverage for a person under 21 years of age.
(c) It shall be unlawful for a person under 21 years of age to exhibit faked, forged, or borrowed credentials in an effort to obtain an alcoholic beverage to which he is not legally entitled.
(d) It shall be unlawful for a person under 21 years of age, other than an employee employed by a licensed person, to have an open container of any alcoholic beverage in his possession.
(e) It shall be a violation for any licensee not to require and properly analyze the identification of a person to ensure that any person under 21 years of age is not sold, served, or has in his possession any alcoholic beverage while in a licensed business or premises; provided that, a licensed employee working in a licensed business or premises may have in his possession any alcoholic beverage for the purpose of selling or serving such alcoholic beverages. The term "identification" as used in this section, shall mean any document issued by a governmental agency containing a description of the person, a photograph, and giving such person's date of birth, and includes, without being limited to, a passport, military identification card, driver's license or state identification card.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
161:
No licensed retail dealer shall purchase any alcoholic beverage from any person other than a licensed wholesale dealer. No licensed wholesale dealer shall sell any alcoholic beverages to any person other than a licensed retail dealer.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
162:
(a) It shall be unlawful for a licensee, his agent or employee to permit any disturbance of the peace, any obscenity, or any lewd, immoral or improper behavior, conduct or practices in the licensed business or premises, or to operate the licensed business or premises in such a manner as to create a nuisance.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any licensee, his agent or employee to fail to report to the city police department any disturbance which occurs immediately outside his business or premises, or in the parking facilities of his business or premises, of which he has knowledge.
(c) It shall be the duty and responsibility of the licensee, his agent, or employee to report to the city police department any usage or possession of illegal drugs or narcotics and to report any unlawful conduct of any nature which occurs on the licensed premises, of which he has knowledge.
(d) It shall be unlawful for any licensee, his agent or employee, to fail to assist any law enforcement officer in the performance of the officer's duties while the officer is in or on a licensed business or premises.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
163:
Consumption or sale of alcoholic beverages in open areas or on decks or patios is not permitted unless a licensee's business or premises is licensed for the retail sale of alcoholic beverages by the drink for consumption on the premises only and such licensee complies with the following regulations:
(1) The open area, patio or deck must be enclosed in a manner that directs ingress and egress by the public through a single entrance only through the licensed business or premises (the purpose of this requirement is to prevent a customer from leaving the open area, patio or deck with an alcoholic beverage without the licensee's knowledge).
(2) The open area, patio or deck shall be enclosed by a structure at least 42 inches in height as measured from the floor of the open area, patio or deck, and such structure must meet all building code requirements of the city.
(3) Any licensee desiring to obtain approval for open area, patio or deck sales must submit to the governing authority a complete set of plans that will be reviewed and approved on an individual basis by governing authority or its designee, and all plans and construction pursuant to such plans shall meet the requirements of the Code, as well as all applicable state health, life safety and fire code. Only upon satisfactory completion of a final inspection will the governing authority approve of any open area, patio or deck sales.
(4) Any structure or area set aside for open area, patio or deck sales shall not contain a number of square feet that represents an amount greater than 40 percent of the existing seating area of the licensed business or premises.
(5) Loudspeakers or other amplifiers of sound shall not be permitted upon the open areas, patios or decks of any licensed business or premises.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
164:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to drink any alcoholic beverages or other intoxicating beverage at any public place within the city, or for any person to have in his possession any unsealed or opened container with such intoxicating beverage in it at any public place within the city, except as may be otherwise temporarily permitted by this chapter or the Code.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to drink or possess any alcoholic beverage upon real property of the city that is used as a public park, playground or school.
(c) It shall be unlawful for any person to drink any alcoholic beverages in any automobile on the streets of the city, whether such automobile shall be moving or parked.
(d) Brown bag establishments shall be prohibited within the city.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
165:
(a) No outdoor advertising promoting the sale or consumption of alcoholic beverages shall be permitted on the exterior of any business or premises that is licensed for wholesale or retail sale of alcoholic beverages or any business or premises that is licensed for the sale of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises only.
(b) Any indoor sign or display promoting the sale or consumption of alcoholic beverages may be visible from the exterior of any business or premises that is licensed for wholesale or retail sale of alcoholic beverages or any business or premises that is licensed for the sale of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises only, subject to the limitations of section 6-25.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
166:
No licensee, or his agent or employee, shall engage in any of the following practices in connection with the sale or other disposition of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises: (a) advertising "Happy Hour" through any form of media, including, but not limited to, newspapers, magazines, electronics, radio, television and internet, or (b) outdoor advertising or signs promoting "Happy Hour" on the exterior of any licensed premises or on the windows or elsewhere on the licensed business or premises that may be viewed from the outside.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
167:
(a) No license shall be issued for the sale of any distilled spirits in or within 100 yards of any church building or within 200 yards of any school building, educational building, school grounds, or college campus.
(b) No license shall be issued for the sale of malt beverage(s) and/or wine by the package for a location that is within 100 yards of any school building, school grounds or college campus (the preceding regulation shall not apply to any location for which a license has been issued prior to July 1, 1981, nor to the renewal of such license, nor shall the preceding regulation apply at any location for which a new license is applied for if the sale of malt beverage(s) and/or wine was lawful at such location at any time during the 12 months immediately preceding such application); provided that, nothing in the preceding regulation shall prohibit a grocery store licensed for the retail sale of only malt beverages and/or wine for consumption off the premises from selling malt beverage(s) and/or wine within 100 yards of any school building, school grounds, or college campus, where so permitted by resolution or ordinance of the county or municipality (as used in this subparagraph, the term "grocery store" means a retail establishment which has a total retail floor space of at least 10,000 square feet of which at least 85 percent is reserved for the sale of food and other nonalcoholic items, conducts all of its sales inside the building containing its retail floor space, and meets such other criteria as may be required by the governing authority.
(c) No license shall be issued for the sale of malt beverage(s) and/or wine by the package for a location that is within 100 yards of any alcoholic treatment center owned and operated by the state or by any county or municipal government (the preceding regulation shall not apply to any business having a license in effect on July 1, 1981).
(d) No license shall be issued for the sale any alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises within 100 yards of any housing authority property (the preceding regulation shall not apply at any location for which a license has been issued prior to July 1, 2000, nor to the renewal of such license, nor shall the preceding regulation apply at any location for which a new license is applied for if the sale of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises was lawful at such location at any time during the 12 months immediately prior to such application; and as used in the preceding regulation, the term "housing authority property" means any property containing 300 housing units or fewer owned or operated by a housing authority created by Article 1 of Chapter 3 of Title 8, the "Housing Authorities Law" of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated).
(e) For purposes of this chapter, distances shall be measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
169:
(a) The business or premises of each licensee shall have a clearly marked point(s) of entry.
(b) The business or premises of each licensee shall have point(s) of entry that are clearly visible from a public street; however, this requirement shall not apply to hotels or where the point of entry of the licensed business or premises is in a shopping center or business building.
(c) The business or premises of each licensee shall ensure that, at all points of entry, there are clear windows and doors. Further, the business or premises of each licensee must maintain clear windows and doors for any cashier's cage within the premises, or other internally enclosed space.
(d) The business or premises of each licensee, including those entirely enclosed in another building, such as a restaurant located in a hotel, must keep all windows and doors free of visual obstructions so that the interior of such business or premises is clearly visible from the exterior. No tinting, shades, curtains, blinds or other devices shall be used to obstruct the view into such business or premises, but tinting, shades, curtains, blinds, and other devices may be used to reduce sun glare so long as such measures do not impede visual access to the business or premises.
(e) The business or premises of each licensee shall operate with an adequate level of internal lighting, so as to ensure visual access from the exterior and safety to law enforcement or other emergency responders, 24 hours, a day seven days a week. External lighting cannot be solely used to meet this requirement.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
170:
(a) No license application shall be considered until the city clerk deems it complete as set forth in this chapter.
(b) If a license application is denied, the applicant for such license cannot apply for another license for a period of six months from the date of the denial.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
172:
(a) A retail dealer of alcoholic beverages by the package may apply for and obtain a Sunday sales license for the retail sale of alcoholic beverages by the package upon due qualification for and payment for such license, as set forth in this chapter.
(b) A retail dealer of alcoholic beverages by the drink for consumption on the premises only may apply for and obtain a Sunday sales license for the retail sale of alcoholic beverages by the drink for consumption on the premises only, upon the occurrence of the following: 1) due qualification for and payment for such license, as set forth in this chapter; and 2) showing to the satisfaction of the city manager, or his designee, that such retail dealer derives at least 50 percent of its total annual gross sales from the sale of prepared meals or food in all of the combined retail outlets of the individual establishments where food is served and in any licensed establishment which derives at least 50 percent of its total annual gross income from the rental of rooms for overnight lodging.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
175:
A license for a retail dealer or wholesale dealer for the sale of beer, malt beverages and/or wine may be granted by the governing authority upon the terms and conditions as provided in this chapter. A license for a retail dealer for the sale of beer, malt beverages and/or wine by the drink for consumption on the premises only may be granted by the governing authority upon the terms and conditions as provided in this chapter.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022; Ord. No. 1916, § I, 6-6-2023)
176:
Before any license permitted under this chapter is granted by the governing authority, the license applicant shall comply with all regulations adopted by the governing authority applicable to such licenses and pay the applicable license fee by certified bank check in an amount set by resolution or ordinance by the governing authority and maintained as a public document by the city clerk.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
177:
(a) There is hereby levied and imposed upon the sale of beer and malt beverages within the city, a specific excise tax as follows:
(1) where beer and malt beverages are sold in or from a barrel or bulk container, a tax of $6.00 on each container sold containing not more than 15½ gallons and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of 15½ gallons; and
(2) where beer and malt beverages are sold in bottles, cans, or other containers, except barrel or bulk containers, a tax of $0.05 per 12 ounces and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of 12 ounces.
(b) The excise taxes provided for in this section shall be imposed upon and shall be paid by the licensed wholesale dealer in beer and malt beverages. Each wholesale dealer selling beer and malt beverages within the city shall file a report with the city by the tenth day of each month showing for the preceding calendar month the exact quantities of beer and malt beverages, by size and type of container, sold during the month within the city. Each wholesale dealer shall remit to the clerk on the tenth day of the month after the calendar month in which such sales were made the amount of excise tax due in accordance with this section.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
178:
(a) There is hereby levied and imposed upon the sale of wine within the City, a specific excise tax in the amount of $0.22 per liter and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of a liter.
(b) The taxes imposed by this section shall not be levied with respect to:
(1) Wine sold to and used by established and recognized churches and synagogues for use in sacramental services only;
(2) Any sale of wine which is exempt from taxation by the state under the Constitution of the United States;
(3) Wine sold to persons outside the state for resale or consumption outside the state; or
(4) Wine which contains less than one-half of one percent alcohol.
(c) The excise taxes as provided for in this section shall be imposed upon and paid by the licensed wholesale dealer in wine, and each wholesale dealer of wine within the city shall file a report with the city by the tenth day of each month showing for the preceding calendar month the exact quantities of wine, by size and type of container, sold during the month within the city. Each wholesale dealer shall remit to the city on the tenth day of the month after the calendar month in which such sales were made the amount of excise tax due in accordance with section 6-52(b).
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
179:
Beer, malt beverages and/or wine shall not be distributed, sold or possessed for the purposes of sale without a license granted by the governing authority. A separate application must be made, and a separate license must be obtained, to sell beer, malt beverages and/or wine for each premises where beer, malt beverages and/or wine is sold at retail or wholesale, or where beer, malt beverages and/or wine is sold at retail by the drink for consumption on the premises only.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022)
180:
A license for the retail sale of beer, malt beverages and/or wine by the drink for consumption on the premises only may only be issued to a: i) restaurant, as described in section 6-2, or ii) retail business, other than a restaurant, that shows, to the satisfaction of the city manager, or his or her designee, that such business derives no less than 65 percent of its total annual gross sales from the sale of such business's goods, products, inventory or services, other than alcoholic beverages, at its premises. Further, the license contemplated herein may only be issued to a restaurant or retail business other than a restaurant which is located within a commercial zoning district of the city.
(Ord. No. 1698, § I, 5-3-2022; Ord. No. 1916, § I, 6-6-2023)
181:
(a) Where a license is issued for the retail sale of beer, malt beverages and/or wine by the drink for consumption on the premises only, in conjunction with a restaurant or a retail business other than a restaurant, the licensee of such license shall submit quarterly written reports to the city clerk, as more particularly set forth herein.

(1) For the purposes of this chapter only, the district is defined as follows: A specifically authorized and pedestrian oriented area of the city established by this section, as it may from time to time be amended, that allows those commercial businesses with valid alcohol licenses within such area to sell, dispense and serve open containers for alcoholic beverages for "carry out" or "off-premises" consumption, provided all other laws, rules and ordinances as well as the requirements of this Code section are followed.
(2) Sales of open containers for alcoholic beverages for carry out or off-premises consumption. Within the district, any business licensed to sell and dispense alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises only is authorized to sell and dispense alcoholic beverages for removal from the premises of such business, for carry out or off-premises consumption, so long as the alcoholic beverage is in a shatter proof, open container bearing the city-required printed sticker or other method of identification, the cost of which is the responsibility of such business. No one shall remove more than one such open container, per person, from the premises of such business at a time; provided that, this limitation shall not apply to the sales of sealed containers of alcoholic beverages for consumption off the premises by duly licensed businesses.
(3) Limit to one open container with maximum of 16 fluid ounces. Within the district, an open container in which an alcoholic beverage is sold, dispensed and removed from the premises of the licensed business and carried in public for consumption shall not exceed 16 fluid ounces in size. No person shall possess on the streets and sidewalks, rights-of-way, parking lots, or in any other public place within the district, any open container of alcoholic beverage which can accommodate or hold more than 16 fluid ounces, and no person shall possess more than one such open container at any time.
(4) Shatter proof open containers required. Any business which is licensed to sell and dispense alcoholic beverages under this article shall sell alcoholic beverages in shatter resistant containers. It shall be unlawful within the district for any person to drink or attempt to drink any alcoholic beverage from an open container that may shatter and/or may create a hazard by breaking, or to possess any such container on the streets, sidewalks, rights-of-way, and/or parking lots within the district, or in any other public place within the district. Patrons, guests or members of the premises of any business which is duly licensed to sell and dispense alcoholic beverages under this article shall not exit the such premises with an open container of alcoholic beverage made of glass.
(5) Purchase only from business licensed to sell and dispense alcoholic beverages in the district. Alcoholic beverages consumed pursuant to this article must be purchased from a business licensed to sell and dispense alcoholic beverages within the district. No alcoholic beverage purchased or brought from outside of the district shall be allowed in an open container in the district.
(6) Prohibitions and limits regarding open containers purchased within district. All alcoholic beverages purchased and/or carried in an open container pursuant to this article shall not be consumed outside of the district. No alcohol may be taken into or onto the premises of any business which is open to the public within the district unless the alcoholic beverage is in an open container that was purchased from the same premises of the business licensed pursuant to this article. Nothing in this article shall be construed to allow the possession or consumption of alcoholic beverages upon any sidewalk adjacent to a church or school or in city parks or recreation buildings unless such areas are the subject of a special event permit approved by the governing authority.
(7) Lawful hours for open containers. Unless otherwise authorized by a special event permit approved by the governing authority, and notwithstanding anything else in the Code to the contrary, the public carrying or consumption of alcoholic beverages in the district will be permitted only during events sanctioned by the governing authority in connection with Lyons Main Street, and only between the hours of 4:00 p.m. and 10:00 p.m. on Thursdays and Fridays and 12:30 p.m. and 11:00 p.m. on Saturdays.
(8) Signage. Any business licensed to sell and dispense alcoholic beverages within the district as permitted by this article that allows guests, members or patrons to leave its premises with an open container of alcoholic beverage shall have prominently displayed at its premises a sign, of a minimum size of eight and one-half inches by 11 inches, for public view a map of the district, with words consisting of the following: "All guests, members and/or patrons leaving this business with an alcoholic beverage do hereby take full responsibility to only carry and consume an alcoholic beverage served in a clear shatter proof container not to exceed 16 oz. in size and obtained by an business licensed to sell alcoholic beverages within the District, as shown in this map. Any individual who leaves the District with alcoholic beverage in an open container is in violation of the City Code and may be subject to prosecution, including jail, probation and/or a fine."
(9) Consumption of alcoholic beverages in a motor vehicle prohibited. It shall be unlawful for any person to consume any alcoholic beverages while in the confines of a motor vehicle while the motor vehicle is located upon any public street, parking lot or other place to which the public has or is permitted to have access within the district.

Animal at large means an animal not under restraint.
Animal control center means the facility designated by the city manager for the detention of animals.

Animal under restraint means any animal:

(3) Confined within a parked vehicle or a vehicle in motion.

Guard dog means any dog which has been trained to attack persons or other animals independently or upon oral command or any dog which, while not so trained, is reasonably expected to perform as a guardian of the property upon and within which it is located.
Owner means any person owning, possessing, keeping, harboring or acting as custodian of a domesticated animal.

276:
(a) The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Commercial means any type of building other than residential.
Construction means the erection of a new building or the alteration of an existing building in connection with its repair or renovation or in connection with making an addition to an existing building and includes the replacement of a malfunctioning, unserviceable, or obsolete faucet, showerhead, toilet or urinal in an existing building.
Residential means any building or unit of a building intended for occupancy as a dwelling, but does not include a hotel or motel.
(b) There shall not be initiated within this city the construction of any residential building of any type which:
(1) Employs a gravity tank-type, flushometer-valve or flushometer-tank toilet that uses more than an average of 1.6 gallons of water per flush;
(2) Employs a showerhead that allows a flow of more than an average of 2.5 gallons of water per minute at 60 pounds per square inch of pressure;
(3) Employs a urinal that uses more than an average of 1.0 gallon of water per flush;
(4) Employs a lavatory faucet or lavatory replacement aerator that allows a flow of more than 2.0 gallons of water per minute; or
(5) Employs a kitchen faucet or kitchen replacement aerator that allows a flow of more than 2.5 gallons of water per minute.
(c) There shall not be initiated within this city the construction of any commercial building of any type which does not meet the requirements of subsections (b)(1) through (5) of this section.
(d) The requirements of subsection (b) of this section shall apply to any residential construction initiated after April 1, 1992, and to any commercial construction initiated after July 1, 1992, which involves the repair or renovation of or addition to any existing building when such repair or renovation of or addition to such existing building includes the replacement of toilets or showers or both.
(e) The requirements of subsections (b), (c) and (d) of this section, relative to new construction and to the repair or renovation of an existing building, shall apply under the following conditions:
(1) When the repair or renovation of the existing building does not include the replacement of the plumbing or sewer system servicing toilets, faucets or showerheads within such existing building;
(2) When such plumbing or sewer system within such existing building, because of its capacity, design or installation, would not function properly if the toilets, faucets or showerheads required by this section were installed;
(3) When such system is a well or gravity flow from a spring and is owned privately by an individual for use in such individual's personal residence; or
(4) When units to be installed are:
a. Specifically designed for use by persons with disabilities;
b. Specifically designed to withstand unusual abuse or installation in a penal institution; or
c. Toilets for juveniles.
(f) The owner or his agent of a building undergoing new construction or repair or renovation who is entitled to an exemption as specified in subsection (e)(2), (3) or (4) of this section shall obtain the exemption by applying at the office of the building inspector. A fee of $25.00 shall be charged for the inspection and issuance of such exemption.
(g) This section shall not apply to any construction of a residential building, the contract for which was entered into prior to April 1, 1992, and shall not apply to any construction of a commercial building, the contract for which was entered into prior to July 1, 1992.
(h) Any person who installs any toilet, faucet, urinal, or showerhead in violation of this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
(i) The sale of a gravity tank-type, flushometer-valve or flushometer-tank toilet that uses more than an average of 1.6 gallons of water per flush shall be prohibited.
(j) This section shall be enforced by the building inspector. Citations for violations may be issued by the chief building inspector.
(Ord. of 7-14-2015(1))
